title: Help
summary: The consumer Help hub uses the Help header, a search trigger, top tasks and short topic paths in comfortable prose.
compare: Help header has a Help tag, Search help and Your library, but no door tabs.
Top tasks use reader language and categories are organized by the task groups.
Comfortable prose is 16/26 and interactive phone controls remain usable.

designReview.reviewer: ResumeDocsWave.DocsMockupLensReview: one reviewer agent, consumer, developer and brand lenses in a single pass

lenses.consumer: Walked in the combined pass; no finding raised for this screen.
lenses.developer: Walked in the combined pass; no finding raised for this screen.
lenses.brand: Walked in the combined pass; 1 finding(s) raised, applied below.

designReview.verdict: Combined three-lens pass ended PASS after its findings were applied; the PR #65 fix round (below) is checked by the contract check only, not re-reviewed by a lens.

findings.issue: The home title inherited the 24/32 article heading instead of the home display step.
findings.resolution: Scoped home titles to 40/48 on desktop and 30/36 on phone, retaining the comfortable-prose body treatment.

findings.issue: Top tasks showed three tiles; plan §8.4 specifies six task tiles.
findings.resolution: Added Download your app, Your code didn’t arrive and Refunds, the same six tiles as docs.landing; the categories and the one Get help with an app line are unchanged.

designReview.notRun: Plan §8.4 and the DOC-01 brief ask for three separate pkey-ux-reviewer passes (consumer, developer, brand consistency). Those three separate passes were not run. One reviewer agent (ResumeDocsWave.DocsMockupLensReview) walked the three lenses as sections of a single pass over saved renders, then re-checked after fixes. The PR #65 fixes recorded above were verified with tools/mockups/check.mjs and shoot.mjs --check only; no lens re-review followed them.
